Article Title: In 2013, Canadian teenager Ann Makosinski invented a flashlight powered by body heat; now she is creating colourful toys to teach children about renewable energy
Article Text:
A new kind of light

eDrink : A mug that generates electricity

Toys with renewable energy

They say some children are born prodigies, and when it comes to Ann Makosinski, the statement holds true. As a teenager living in Canada, her friend living in the Philippines told her that she couldn't study at night since her family couldn't afford electricity to turn the lights on. Soon she wondered if there was a way to have light without traditional electricity. This is when she came up with a record-making invention, a flashlight powered by body heat.Like other children her age, Makosinski did not watch television or play video games. She spent her time listening to the opera, watching silent movies and learning to play the piano and violin. Interestingly, her first toy was a box of transistors. “I wasn’t given many toys, so I had to make my own,” she said to CNN back in 2019. “I would take garbage and my hot glue gun from around the house and piece together these so-called inventions, and obviously they never worked, but the idea of taking things from around me and piecing them together to make something better just kind of came really naturally. ”Makosinski was only 15 when she invented a flashlight that was powered by the heat of the user's hands.The Hollow Flashlight uses thermoelectric technology to convert the temperature difference between the user's hand and the surrounding air into electricity. The device uses Peltier tiles, which generate electricity when one side is heated by the palm of the hand and the other is cooled.No batteries are required, with the flashlight running entirely on human body heat that would otherwise go to waste. School students, therefore, could study without worrying about running out of battery power.The Hollow Flashlight earned Makosinski a win in the 15-16 age category at the 2013 Google Science Fair and won at the 2014 Intel International Science and Engineering Fair. Her wins made her an international media sensation. She made appearances on shows such as 'The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon' and was featured in publications such as TIME and Forbes. She even gave a TEDxTeen Talk titled 'Why I don't use a smartphone'. Makosinski only bought her first phone, an old-fashioned flip model, at the age of 18.The intrigued teenager did not stop there. Soon, she launched her next major invention, the eDrink. At 18, while enrolled at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, she designed a coffee mug to capture the excess heat from a hot beverage and convert it into electricity. This excess energy could then be used to provide a small charge to a phone or other device for 30 minutes. It uses Peltier tiles (thermoelectric generators), and by heating one side of the tiles with your drink and cooling the other side with the design of the mug (and a bunch of electronic circuits, of course), electricity is produced."I got the inspiration for my project when I noticed that my high school friends were always complaining about their phones dying too soon and that their coffee was too hot to drink," she told Society for Science.Now 29, Makosinski is looking to inspire other young girls across the world to use their minds and creativity in a similar fashion. Her interest in thermoelectric technology has led her toward a different kind of invention: toys designed to teach children about renewable energy.She has created bright-coloured toys that help kids learn about renewable energy in exciting ways. They can see and play with it as it lights up, spins or makes sound when powered by sunlight, water or a hand-wound mechanism.The goal now, she told CNN, is to have other youngsters, girls in particular, follow her into the world of science.“I just want, especially young kids, to feel like they can invent their own solutions and they don’t have to wait for other people to make them,” said Makosinski, who described herself as “a normal girl who just used her time differently after school.”“I want to inspire people to be more creative with the resources they have around them,” she added.
Article Summary: Ann Makosinski was 15 when she invented a flashlight powered by body heat. At 18, she designed a coffee mug to capture excess heat from a hot beverage and convert it into electricity. Now 29, she is looking to inspire other young girls across the world to use their minds and creativity.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to engineers: Use AI but never ...
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to engineers: Use AI but never ...

Engineer says AI is changing software development

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has warned engineers against relying too heavily on artificial intelligence for software development. In an X post, Sridhar Vembu said that engineers should use AI tools without giving up their own understanding of the work. Vembu was responding to a post by a software engineer who described the use of Anthropic's Claude Code at a large company. The engineer claimed that AI was being used to create almost every part of the software development process, including specifications, code, tests, product requirement documents (PRDs), tickets and reports."Nobody knows anything here. The specs, code, tests, PRDs, tickets, resolution of those tickets, reports, etc., everything is made by Claude Code. Nobody on my team likes this. They are being forced to ship as much as they can," the engineer wrote.Sridhar Vembu quoted and replied “This is sad. I tell our engineers to use AI but never cede our understanding to AI”. He also warned that companies may be adopting AI-powered coding tools faster than engineers can understand their impact.“As an industry, we are driving too fast in a fancy new car we barely understand how to drive, inviting disaster,” Vembu stated.The engineer's post also raised concerns about the pressure to deliver more code as AI makes software development faster. According to the post, employees were working 12 to 13 hours a day while spending much of their time directing AI tools instead of writing or understanding code themselves. The engineer said there was little time to inspect what the AI had produced or understand how different parts of the system worked.“People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter,” the engineer wrote.“There is no sense of victory. Nobody is resolving bugs. In reality, nobody is thinking anymore. Everything is done by LLMs. It is so soul-sucking. I would not mind it, to be honest, if we were at least given the time to check out the code and see what is going where. But no, the goal is to just ship. No matter what happens,” the engineer wrote.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has warned engineers against relying too heavily on artificial intelligence for software development. He was responding to a post by a software engineer who described the use of Anthropic's Claude Code at a large company. The engineer claimed that AI was being used to create almost every part of the software development process.

Article Title: Amazon blocks Meta's AI Agent Muse AI on its app, unhappy with Facebook-parent capturing and storing customer credentials; says, 'never told us that ...'
Article Text:
Meta’s position on credential security

Amazon has reportedly blocked Meta’s new autonomous personal assistant, Muse, from navigating and purchasing products on Amazon.com on behalf of shoppers. The restriction follows unsuccessful attempts by the retail giant to convince Facebook’s parent company to voluntarily drop Amazon from the artificial intelligence (AI) tool’s automated shopping routines. Last year, Amazon sent a cease-and-desist letter to Perplexity, asking the company to stop their bots and that the e-tailer does not want to be part of Comet browser.GeekWire reported that Amazon said it never consented to the integration. It added that Meta launched the feature without advance notice, designed the agent to browse without identifying itself as automated software, and appears to harvest and retain customer credentials, a combination Amazon warns poses serious privacy and security hazards.By Sunday (September 20) night, consumers attempting to use Muse for purchases on Amazon encountered an explicit roadblock message: “Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.”According to the report, an Amazon spokesperson emphasized that external platforms should adhere to basic commercial boundaries:“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate.”Meta has previously rejected allegations that its agent mishandles sensitive user information. The parent company of Facebook and Instagram noted that Muse operates without direct visibility into user passwords or banking details. It also stated that any log-in information entered by a consumer is placed into protected storage, enabling the model to utilise credentials without reading them directly, even when an individual types them straight into a browser session.The clash creates an awkward rift between two longstanding commercial allies. Since 2023, Amazon has allowed consumers to buy products directly within Facebook and Instagram feeds. In April, Meta inked a multibillion-dollar contract to run its autonomous AI agents using Amazon's custom Graviton server chips.The report said that the friction exposes a wider battle over which tech firm maintains ownership of the shopper relationship as automated agents begin executing digital commerce on behalf of people.
Article Summary: Amazon blocks Meta’s new autonomous personal assistant, Muse, from navigating and purchasing products on Amazon.com on behalf of shoppers. Amazon said it never consented to the integration. It added that Meta launched the feature without advance notice, designed the agent to browse without identifying itself as automated software, and appears to retain customer credentials.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.

Article Title: IIT Palakkad researchers develop camera-free sensor for safer driving
Article Text:
The sensor system detects electrical signals generated by human touch to determine the position of the driver’s hands on the steering wheel

Palakkad

:





Researchers at IIT Palakkad have developed a touch-sensing system that can detect hand positions and grip patterns on a vehicle’s steering wheel without using cameras.The system, developed by associate professor Sreenath Vijayakumar and technical superintendent Pinku Sebastian from the institute’s department of electrical engineering, is aimed at improving driver safety while addressing privacy concerns associated with camera-based monitoring.The sensor system uses thin sensor strips placed on surfaces such as steering wheels. It detects electrical signals generated by human touch to determine the position of the driver’s hands.The team developed a prototype steering wheel fitted with the sensors and tested its performance under different conditions. According to the researchers, the system can detect hand positions with high precision and works in darkness, bright sunlight and varying weather conditions.“Without needing visual images, the interface can instantly detect where exactly your hands are placed around the wheel, how firmly or lightly you are holding it and whether you are driving with two hands, one hand, or no hands for an extended period of time,” said Vijayakumar.The researchers said the technology could be used to provide warnings when unsafe one-handed driving, distraction or fatigue is detected.Unlike camera-based systems, the touch-sensing technology does not capture images of the driver or surroundings and is designed to be lightweight and relatively inexpensive.According to researchers, the technology also has potential applications beyond automobiles and it could be used in helper robots to detect human contact and in smart ICU beds to monitor patient movements and weight shifts and alert healthcare staff to possible fall risks.
Article Summary: The system uses thin sensor strips placed on surfaces such as steering wheels. It detects electrical signals generated by human touch to determine the position of the driver’s hands. The technology could be used to provide warnings when unsafe one-handed driving, distraction or fatigue is detected.

Article Title: Indonesia replanted mangroves on Flores in 2013; 10 years later, restored forests supported 10 fauna species and stored up to 70 Mg CO2 per hectare
Article Text:
Image AI generated

What did scientists find in Indonesia’s replanted Flores mangroves

Mangrove restoration stored up to 70.02 Mg CO2 per hectare

Image AI generated

Mangrove species varied across Flores restoration sites

Indonesia’s Flores Island was the site of a mangrove reforestation project launched in 2013, with native seedlings planted along the coast between Ende and Sikka. Ten years later, researchers surveyed restored areas at Bangkoor, Kolisia and Talibura to assess plant and animal diversity, carbon sequestration and energy storage. The study recorded 10 mangrove species and 10 fauna species across the three sites. Kolisia had the highest mangrove species richness, while Talibura had the highest fauna species richness. Restored stands also recorded carbon sequestration, although the researchers found differences in vegetation development between the three locations after a decade.According to the study published in Scientific Reports titled ‘ Mangroves, fauna compositions and carbon sequestration after ten years restoration on Flores Island, Indonesia ’, the survey identified 10 mangrove species from six families across the three locations. Kolisia recorded the highest plant species richness, with eight species, followed by Bangkoor with seven and Talibura with five. The study found that Kolisia had the highest vegetation diversity, while Talibura had a large number of seedlings and saplings.The researchers also identified 10 fauna species across the three reforestation sites. Talibura recorded the highest fauna species richness, with eight species, followed by Bangkoor with seven and Kolisia with six.The animals included the crab-eating macaque (Macaca fascicularis), which the study lists as endangered, along with mudskippers, bivalves, crabs, gastropods, reptiles and birds.After 10 years of reforestation, carbon sequestration in the restored mangrove stands ranged from 28.69 to 70.02 Mg CO2 per hectare. Energy storage ranged from 30.54 × 10⁴ to 54.07 × 10⁴ MJ per hectare. These figures were calculated for Bangkoor and Kolisia because no poles or trees were recorded at Talibura during the assessment.At species level, Rhizophora apiculata had the highest carbon sequestration value, at 47.37 ± 5.68 kg CO2. Bruguiera gymnorhiza recorded the highest energy storage value, at 645.22 ± 201.65 MJ. The researchers estimated carbon and energy storage using above-ground biomass rather than destructive sampling. Carbon storage was calculated using a factor of 0.47.The researchers found similarities in plant and animal communities between the three restoration sites, although some species occurred only at particular locations. Avicennia marina was recorded only at Kolisia, while Excoecaria agallocha and Lumnitzera rasemosa were recorded only at Bangkoor. Among the animals, Varanus salvator was recorded at Kolisia, while Macaca fascicularis was recorded at Bangkoor.The study found differences in the development of the restored mangroves after 10 years. The researchers reported relatively low levels of species richness, heterogeneity and evenness across the mangrove ecosystems. Talibura had the greatest water depth of the three sites, fewer mangrove species and no poles or trees recorded during the survey. The researchers recommended continued long-term monitoring of mangrove health, resilience and ecological changes.
Article Summary: Mangrove restoration stored up to 70.02 Mg CO2 per hectare. Kolisia had the highest vegetation diversity, while Talibura had a large number of seedlings and saplings. The study recorded 10 mangrove species and 10 fauna species across the three sites.

Article Title: Two New York brothers started experimenting with CNC machining in their parents' garage; today, they run a high-tech company making parts for aerospace and medical industries
Article Text:
Brothers Sean (left) and James (right) Cerven launched Cerven Solutions from their parents' garage in 2020 (Image: HVMFG)

How two New York brothers turned a garage experiment into a high-tech company

Co-Founder Sean Cerven cutting bar stock to the required dimensions (Image: HVMFG)

Making precision components for specialised industries

Working with challenging materials

Two brothers from New York transformed a pandemic-era experiment in their parents' garage into a precision manufacturing business serving technically demanding industries. Sean and James Cerven began learning CNC machining in 2020 after purchasing a Tormach PCNC 440 milling machine. Working from their parents' garage in Poughkeepsie, they initially took on small jobs that helped them gain practical experience. As their interest in machining developed into a long-term business ambition, they established Cerven Solutions. The company later expanded beyond its garage workshop, joined the Xometry Partner Network and invested in advanced machinery and inspection equipment. Today, it produces complex, precision-machined components for the aerospace, defence, radar and satellite communications sectors.During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, mechanical engineering students James and Sean Cerven began learning about CNC machining. The process uses computer-controlled machines to cut, drill and shape materials such as metal and plastic according to digital designs.After purchasing a Tormach PCNC 440 milling machine, the brothers began experimenting in their parents' garage in Poughkeepsie, New York.They initially received small jobs from customers, giving them an opportunity to build practical experience despite their limited background in commercial machining.As they became more familiar with designing and manufacturing components, the brothers realised they wanted to pursue machining professionally. They began developing their project into Cerven Solutions, turning their technical interests into a commercial manufacturing venture.While looking for additional customers, the brothers discovered Xometry through a machining group on Facebook. They contacted the company and subsequently purchased additional tooling and inspection equipment. After completing a test part, they joined the Xometry Partner Network, which connected them with potential manufacturing projects.The company soon outgrew its garage workshop as the volume of work increased. In its February 2025 case study, Xometry reported that Cerven Solutions had completed 671 projects through the platform and generated $1.5 million in Xometry revenue. The report also stated that the company had moved into a 3,000-square-foot workshop and was investing in additional machinery and quality-control equipment.Cerven Solutions produces precision-machined components for aerospace, defence, satellite communications and other specialised technology sectors. The company lists capabilities including waveguides, split-block assemblies, RF couplers, power dividers, polarisers, radio-frequency housings, filter bodies and resonator cavities. It also lists antenna structures, optical and sensor housings, thermal-management components such as cold plates and heat spreaders, along with brackets and mounting hardware.For aerospace and unmanned aerial systems, the company lists structural fittings, hardpoints, motor and payload mounts, fins, canards and actuation fittings. Its listed capabilities also include power and battery enclosures, such as module housings, sealed lids and terminal plates. These examples come from Cerven Solutions' official website, which describes the types of hardware it builds rather than identifying specific customer orders.As Cerven Solutions expanded, the brothers invested in equipment designed to improve machining precision and production efficiency. The company's website lists a Matsuura MX-420 PC10 five-axis machining centre, FANUC RoboDrill machines and a Datron neo machining centre.It also lists a Zeiss DuraMax coordinate measuring machine for dimensional inspection. Such equipment allows manufacturers to check whether finished components meet the measurements and tolerances specified in engineering designs.The company works with materials including aluminium, titanium, stainless steel and high-performance plastics. Its website describes capabilities involving thin walls, deep pockets, tight corners and substantial material removal.These machining tasks require careful control because manufacturers must maintain dimensional accuracy while cutting away material. Cerven Solutions says it has developed processes to manage challenges such as chatter, wall taper and material stress when producing complex components. The company also states that it is working towards Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 2 and is not currently certified under that standard.Sean and James Cerven began with a CNC milling machine in their parents' garage and initially relied on small customer jobs to build experience. As their confidence and ambitions grew, they developed the project into Cerven Solutions and explored ways to secure more manufacturing work.
Article Summary: Brothers Sean and James Cerven began learning CNC machining in 2020. They began experimenting in their parents' garage in Poughkeepsie, New York. As their interest in machining developed into a long-term business ambition, they established Cerven Solutions. The company produces precision-machined components for aerospace, defence, radar and satellite communications sectors.

Article Title: In 2007, an Australian geologist browsing Google Earth spotted an 850-foot circle in the outback; drilling later confirmed an iron-meteorite crater
Article Text:
AI Representation: An Australian geologist browsing Google Earth spotted an 850-foot circle in the outback. Image credits: Chatgpt

A 260-metre crater in the Pilbara

What the 2008 paper concluded

Hickman Crater, Ophthalmia Range, Western Australia: evidence supporting a

meteorite impact

origin

Why GSWA drilled in 2012

Meteor crater. Image credits: Wikipedia

Why the impact left little shock damage

In July 2007, a geologist scrolling through satellite images of Western Australia noticed a near-perfect circle in the outback. At the time, Arthur Hickman of the Geological Survey of Western Australia did not know he was looking at an impact crater, one that was later found to be among the youngest in Australia.A study from the Australian Journal of Earth Sciences found that the size of the structure was around 260 metres (around 850 feet). The structure has been described by Australian Geographic as being the latest meteorite crater structure that has been discovered in Australia. This structure has been informally named the Hickman Crater.The structure was measured at about 260 metres (850 feet) across, making it relatively small compared with many known impact structures. Australian Geographic has described it as the latest meteorite crater structure discovered in Australia. Informally known as the Hickman Crater, it adds another possible impact site to the country’s growing record of meteorite-related geological structures.The first detailed published analysis came in the paper, published in the Australian Journal of Earth Sciences . Authors Glikson, Hickman and Vickers reported a mean crater diameter of 260 metres.The lack of fragments from young volcanics younger than the Woongarra Rhyolite was not consistent with the explosive volcanic mechanism. Instead, the authors concluded that an impact had occurred, likely from a projectile about 10 metres wide that excavated a crater roughly 80 metres deep. It was dated to the Late Pleistocene period, with an age of between 10,000 and 100,000 years, due to the damming effect of the southern margin on a nearby creek.Field evidence was not enough to raise a certainty. According to a 2017 news release from the Department of Mines, Industry Regulation and Safety (DMIRS), the Geological Survey of Western Australia ran the 2012 drilling project with Atlas Iron, which was already working in the area, to confirm early suspicions that the structure was a meteorite impact crater. Those results are laid out in the study Collaborative scientific drilling at Hickman Crater by P. W. Haines. The study describes a circular rim about 260 metres across that rises to 30 metres above a flat floor. The depth of the hole, drilled vertically in the aforementioned floor, was 64.7 metres. According to the 2012 drill core, the upper 48.4 metres is sediment that accumulated in the crater after it formed. At depths between 55.1 and 64.7 meters, there was very fractured rhyolite, which was the original bedrock.The crucial piece of evidence was chemistry. Ratios of platinum group elements in the breccia resembled those of meteorites much more than the ratios in the average continental crust, meaning a considerable meteoritic content. High nickel concentration indicated an iron meteorite. According to Haines, iron projectiles are the most common type to form small, simple craters like this one, even though chondrites are more common among meteorite falls overall, since stony projectiles of this size usually break up in the air.Haines suggests that the projectile, estimated at about 10 metres across, may have been slowed significantly by the atmosphere before impact, which could have reduced shock pressures below the level needed to form the diagnostic planar deformation features while still leaving enough energy to excavate the crater. As has been suggested by Haines, the object may have been small enough to decelerate within the Earth's atmosphere before impact. As noted above, this appears to be the first scientific drill hole in a simple crater less than one kilometre in diameter in Australia, and possibly elsewhere.The atmospheric deceleration could also help explain why the crater's characteristics differ from those expected from a larger, faster impactor. Despite the lack of some conventional impact markers, the crater's size and morphology remain consistent with an impact origin. Further drilling and analysis of the recovered material could provide additional evidence about the event and its formation.
Article Summary: In 2007, a geologist browsing Google Earth spotted an 850-foot circle in the outback of Western Australia. The crater was measured at about 260 metres (850 feet) across, making it relatively small compared with many known impact structures. It was dated to the Late Pleistocene period, with an age of between 10,000 and 100,000 years, due to the damming effect of the southern margin on a nearby creek.

Article Title: US Army built an 11-by-8-foot floating island from recycled plastic bottles; native plants now help clean water and shelter wildlife
Article Text:
How a military wash basin became a testing ground for a floating wetland

Inside the unusual design of the U.S.S. Eddy

How the floating island uses plants to filter water naturally

What happens next for Fort Cavazos' floating island experiment

At a military vehicle wash facility in Texas, an unusual structure is sitting on the surface of a catchment basin. It is only 11 by 8 feet, but its purpose extends beyond simply floating. Known as the U.S.S. Eddy, the prototype was built from corrugated pipes packed with recycled plastic bottles, covered with layers of screening and coconut fibre, then planted with native aquatic vegetation. The idea came from staff at Fort Cavazos who were looking for a way to improve water quality while making use of a basin already attracting fish, turtles, frogs, waterfowl and other wildlife. The floating platform was launched in March 2024, as reported by The US Army.The basin serves a practical military purpose. Tracked vehicles are cleaned with high-pressure water that removes dirt, oil, fluids and other material from their surfaces. Rather than flowing straight away, the wastewater enters the catchment basin, where heavier sediment can settle before the water is recycled for further use.That system leaves the basin holding water containing much finer contaminants as well.The floating island was designed to work within that existing setup rather than replace it.Fort Cavazos' Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization and Security, or DPTMS, developed the project with its Adaptive and Integrative Management Team. The intention was to introduce a biological element into the treatment process, using plants and their growing environment as a natural filter.The setting also offered another reason to experiment. Wildlife was already using the area.The U.S.S Eddy does not resemble a conventional piece of water-treatment equipment. Its base consists of corrugated pipes filled with discarded plastic bottles. Polyester screen cloth and a coconut liner were added above that framework, creating a surface capable of supporting plants.Native horsetails, pennywort and sedges were selected for the planting layer. Rather than simply placing greenery on a floating platform, the design is intended to create a small living system in which the plants can interact with the water around them.The arrangement gives the island several functions at once. As the vegetation grows, the structure can provide places for wildlife to rest and feed while the plants and their surrounding material contribute to filtration and nutrient cycling.For the people involved in the project, that combination was important. The aim was not just to make the basin's water cleaner. It was also to add habitat to a site that wildlife was already visiting.The floating platform was intended to act in much the same way as a small wetland. Water passes around the plant roots and through the material supporting them, creating opportunities for contaminants and excess nutrients to be captured or processed.The project team said the island was particularly aimed at fine, emulsified contaminants in the basin. It was also expected to help reduce algae and improve the quality of the recycled water through natural processes rather than relying entirely on mechanical treatment.That makes the plants more than decoration. Their roots, growth and interaction with the water are central to how the prototype is supposed to work.There is also a practical wildlife benefit. The basin already supports waterfowl, crawfish, fish, turtles and frogs, while coyotes and raccoons have also been observed around the area. The floating structure gives some of those animals another place to shelter or find food.The March 2024 launch was treated as a trial rather than a finished solution. DPTMS and the AIM Team planned to monitor the island over time, looking at how well the design performed and whether parts of it could be changed.That monitoring could cover everything from the performance of the plants to the durability and efficiency of the floating framework. Lessons from the prototype are intended to guide later versions.The longer-term proposal is considerably larger than the first experiment. Fort Cavazos said it hoped eventually to assemble and launch as many as 20 floating islands.For now, the U.S.S. Eddy remains a relatively small structure on a military catchment basin. Its construction, however, combines several simple elements: waste plastic, recycled water, native plants and a platform designed to support wildlife.The experiment is also taking place in a working facility rather than a purpose-built conservation area. That makes the basin itself part of the test, as the team watches how a floating wetland performs alongside the everyday demands of washing military vehicles.
Article Summary: The U.S. Eddy was built from corrugated pipes packed with recycled plastic bottles, covered with layers of screening and coconut fibre. It is then planted with native aquatic vegetation. The idea came from staff at Fort Cavazos who were looking for a way to improve water quality while making use of a basin.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape
Article Text:
From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

From discarded tyres to footwear with a purpose, the idea began with a childhood experience. At the age of 10, UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar visited rural Africa, where he saw children walking long distances barefoot, often without adequate footwear.Moved by what he witnessed, Ahaan gave away his favourite pair of slippers to a child he met during the visit. The experience stayed with him long after he returned home and eventually became the starting point for a larger idea.As he grew older, Ahaan began exploring how discarded materials could be repurposed to address the lack of affordable, durable footwear. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles.The idea brought together two concerns he had encountered separately: the growing problem of tyre waste and the need for accessible footwear.He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala, and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day. Ahaan then connected with Mamco General Trading, which operates in Uganda and Zambia. As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility programme, the company will purchase 4,000 pairs of slippers each month for free distribution to children and families in need. It’s a sustainable cycle that turns waste into opportunity, supporting livelihoods and giving kids durable footwear.“When I was 10 years old, I saw children my age walking barefoot, and I never forgot that moment,” Ahaan says. “I wanted to create something that could help people and the environment. If we can turn discarded tyres into something useful and long-lasting, maybe it can inspire more young people to believe their simple ideas can really make a difference.”The world’s growing dependence on convenience and mobility comes with an environmental cost. Every year, more than a billion tyres reach the end of their usable life, creating a significant waste-management challenge. Many of these tyres end up in landfills, while others are burned or processed in ways that can contribute to pollution and the loss of valuable materials.Repurposing discarded tyres offers one way to address this challenge by keeping materials in use for longer and reducing the amount of waste that needs to be disposed of. Turning old tyres into durable slipper soles, for instance, gives a material that would otherwise be discarded a new application while also reducing the need for virgin raw materials in footwear production.The approach reflects a broader shift in how sustainability is being understood. Rather than treating waste simply as something to be collected and discarded, initiatives like this explore how materials already in circulation can be redesigned and put to practical use.In doing so, they can support waste reduction, resource conservation and efforts to lower the environmental impact associated with new production. Ultimately, sustainability is not only about recycling what has already been used, but also about rethinking waste as a potential resource.
Article Summary: UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar saw children walking barefoot in rural Africa. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles. He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day.

Article Title: Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott: “The leadership of people directly experiencing inequities is essential, both because…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott

“The leadership of people directly experiencing inequities is essential, both because it is informed by insights no one else can contribute, and because it seeds power and opportunity within the community itself.”

What is the meaning behind today’s quote by MacKenzie Scott

What MacKenzie Scott means by leadership from lived experience

When support means giving others the power to lead

What the quote says about decision-making

How to turn the quote into everyday action

Listen before deciding: Ask people affected by a decision what they actually need.

Give people a real say: Listening has more value when their views can influence what happens next.

Share responsibility: When working with others, let them take ownership instead of making every decision yourself.

Trust people with experience: People who deal with a problem directly may understand practical solutions better than outsiders.

Move beyond asking for opinions: If you ask someone for input, consider giving them a role in shaping the outcome.

Make space for others to lead: Leadership does not always have to come from the person with the most authority.

Share control where possible: In family, work or community decisions, involve the people who will be directly affected.

Measure success together: Ask those involved whether a decision or solution actually worked, rather than judging it alone.

Turn listening into action: The lesson is not simply to hear people, but to let what you hear influence your decisions.

Some of the people best placed to describe a problem are not always the people invited to design its solution. That gap appears in many areas of public life, from education and healthcare to housing and economic opportunity. MacKenzie Scott has built much of her philanthropic approach around a related question: what happens when the people living with a problem are given more say in deciding how it should be addressed? In a 2022 essay, Scott wrote about the importance of supporting leaders with direct experience of inequity. Her observation was not simply about representation. It was also about knowledge, responsibility and where power sits when decisions are made on behalf of a community.Scott included the line in her March 2022 essay Helping Any of Us Can Help Us All. She was discussing her approach to giving and the importance of hearing from people whose lives are directly affected by the issues that organisations are trying to address.The wording makes two separate points. The first is about knowledge. Someone who has lived through a particular barrier may notice things that are invisible from outside it. The second is about power. When people from the affected community take leadership roles, resources and decision-making ability can remain within that community rather than being controlled entirely by outside institutions.Scott is not arguing that personal experience is the only qualification for leadership. Her wider writing points instead towards a broader principle: people who understand an issue through their own lives should have meaningful influence over the response to it.A charity working with people facing poverty, for example, may understand statistics about income, housing or employment. Someone who has personally moved between temporary accommodation and insecure work brings a different kind of information. They may know where a system becomes difficult to navigate, which requirements create unnecessary barriers, or why an apparently useful service is rarely used.Neither form of knowledge automatically replaces the other. Scott's argument is that one should not be treated as sufficient while the other is ignored.The phrase “seeds power and opportunity” takes the argument beyond consultation.There is a difference between asking people for their views and giving them the authority to act on those views. A community can be invited to a meeting, asked to complete a survey or consulted during the design of a programme without having much influence over what happens afterwards. Leadership is different because it changes who is making decisions.That is particularly relevant to philanthropy, where large institutions or wealthy donors can have substantial control over which problems receive money and which approaches are considered worth supporting. Scott has repeatedly written about moving some of that control towards the organisations receiving funding.In a 2021 essay titled 'Seeding by Ceding', she argued that people dealing directly with inequities deserved greater attention in stories about the change they were creating. She also wrote that solutions were best designed and implemented by others rather than centred on the donors providing the money.There is a practical question hidden inside Scott's words: who gets to decide what a community needs? It is easy for outside institutions to define a problem from a distance. A funding body might describe a community through poverty rates, health statistics, educational outcomes or other measurements. Those numbers can be useful, but they cannot capture every detail of how people experience a system.A person who has lived with the problem can bring another layer of information. That does not make lived experience automatically correct. Personal experience can be partial, just as institutional data can be incomplete. The point is about the value of having both perspectives in the room, particularly when decisions affect the people whose lives are being discussed.Scott's approach places particular weight on the second perspective because it is often the one with less access to money and institutional authority.
Article Summary: MacKenzie Scott wrote about the importance of supporting leaders with direct experience of inequity in 2022 essay Helping Any of Us Can Help Us All. She was discussing her approach to giving and importance of hearing from people whose lives are directly affected by the issues that organisations are trying to address.

Article Title: Apple executive reveals why he hates screen protectors: It makes my skin crawl because …
Article Text:
Apple executive reveals why he hates screen protectors: It makes my skin crawl because …

Apple wants iPhone screens to last longer

Apple says it tests screens for years of use

Many iPhone users put a screen protector on their phones as soon as they take them out of the box. But one Apple executive has admitted that seeing a screen protector on an iPhone is not something he likes. Tom Marieb, Apple ’s vice president of hardware engineering (the role that current CEO John Ternus once held), explained why during a recent group interview while discussing the company’s latest work on display durability. “Personally, when I see someone put a screen protector on their iPhone, it makes my skin crawl, because we work so hard to make beautiful front screens,” Marieb said.Tom Marieb said Apple has been working on new coatings that can protect the display from scratches while also making the surface resistant to wear over time. The two goals can be difficult to achieve together, he explained.“We worry about scratching, which is obviously very dependent on having [material that can withstand] very sharp things going into the screen. But we also worry about wear over time; as people use the screen, whether they’ll wear away that surface.”According to Marieb, Apple tried to find a balance between scratch resistance and long-term durability with Ceramic Shield 2.“We could have made it more scratch-resistant, but it would have been a little less wear-resistant. It’s the long life we’re looking for against both of those loads over time.”Apple's approach is not simply to test how a screen performs when it is new. Tom Marieb said the company tries to recreate how people actually use their phones in everyday life. “We very much try to meet the customer where they live,” he said.Apple also uses accelerated testing to simulate years of use in a much shorter period. Marieb said the company can represent five years of use, or even more, within a couple of weeks of testing.“And as you said, people waiting a year or two to actually see the benefits of [Ceramic Shield 2] means we've correctly predicted how people would use it,” he said.
Article Summary: Tom Marieb said Apple has been working on new coatings that can protect the display from scratches while also making the surface resistant to wear over time. Marieb: “When I see someone put a screen protector on their iPhone, it makes my skin crawl, because we work so hard to make beautiful front screens”

Article Title: When a district in Florida used robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons and protect Everglades
Article Text:
How Florida’s AI-powered robot rabbits work

Why Florida is targeting Burmese pythons

Florida Python Challenge adds to python removal efforts

Florida used an unusual tool to control the growing population of invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades: solar-powered robot rabbits. In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida teamed up to deploy robotic rabbit decoys designed to mimic real prey and lure pythons out of hiding using artificial intelligence (AI), heat signatures and scent simulation.The robots are part of Florida’s broader effort to remove Burmese pythons, which have disrupted native wildlife populations across the state. The devices use AI-powered cameras to detect approaching snakes and alert officials, who can then send trained python removal agents to capture and remove them. The technology is being used alongside the annual Florida Python Challenge and other removal programmes, not replacing them.The solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes, which use thermal sensing and smell while hunting. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts South Florida Water Management District officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.The district and University of Florida are deploying the robots at sites across South Florida where pythons are known to hide. The approach is intended to help monitor areas that can be difficult to survey using conventional methods. It also gives wildlife officials another way to locate snakes in areas where dense vegetation and difficult terrain can limit traditional searches.“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district noted.Burmese pythons were introduced into the Everglades during the 1970s and have since become an invasive predator in Florida. Researchers estimate that between 100,000 and 300,000 Burmese pythons are present across the state’s subtropical regions. The snakes can grow longer than 18 feet, and adult females can lay more than 70 eggs in a single clutch. Their presence has affected native mammals, birds and reptiles, reducing available prey for species including Florida panthers, bobcats and birds of prey.​A 2012 US Geological Survey study found that raccoon and opossum populations in parts of the Everglades had declined by nearly 99% following the spread of Burmese pythons.Florida has also relied on trained contractors and public participation to remove Burmese pythons. The annual Florida Python Challenge brings professional and amateur hunters together for a 10-day competition, and participants must complete a safety course before taking part. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, collectively removed 280 Burmese pythons. The competition's overall tally has now exceeded 1,600 snakes.Tom Rahill won the $10,000 grand prize after removing 96 snakes, while Rahm Levinson received $1,000 for capturing the longest python, measuring 16 feet, five inches. Additional prizes were awarded across professional, novice and military categories.​“The number of invasive pythons removed from the Everglades during the 2026 Florida Python Challenge is a major victory for Florida’s native wildlife and a testament to what can be accomplished through strong partnerships and public participation,” FWC chairman Rodney Barreto said in a statement.Since 2017, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and South Florida Water Management District contractors have removed more than 19,000 snakes. The district's robotic rabbit programme is intended to add another method to those ongoing efforts.
Article Summary: The robots are designed to imitate prey Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.

Article Title: Month after laying off hundreds in Siri and Vision team, Apple cuts jobs in Fitness+; affected staff include …
Article Text:
Month after laying off hundreds in Siri and Vision team, Apple cuts jobs in Fitness+; affected staff include …

Apple job cuts : Staff impacted

Apple laid off employees in Siri and Vision Pro team last month

Apple has reportedly laid off staff working on Fitness+, reports Bloomberg. In the weekly Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman said that the job cuts indicate “hanging priorities for the service”, adding that the iPhone maker was previously “reevaluating its Fitness+ platform, a competitor to Peloton content that’s now overseen by services chief Eddy Cue and health leader Sumbul Desai”. “This past week, I’m told, Apple enacted another round of increasingly common layoffs by cutting a handful of employees working on Fitness+,” Gurman said in the newsletter.The reported job cuts come a month after laid off more than 200 people across the teams building Siri and the Vision Pro last month.As stated in the newsletter, the affected workers included staff who contributed to the audio side of the service — things like the Time to Walk and Time to Run audio sessions you can listen to from your Apple Watch without watching a video. Gurman noted that new releases for audio content will drop in frequency, but “they’re not going away completely — as of now”.In August, Gurman reported that Apple cut more than 200 people across the teams building Siri and the Vision Pro, according to a Bloomberg report by Mark Gurman. The split is roughly even. About 100 roles have gone from the Vision Pro organisation, and about 100 more from Siri and the software groups around it.Also caught in the round is Intelligent Systems Experience, a team inside Apple's software engineering arm that builds AI features sitting across iPhone, iPad and Mac.Apple confirmed the cuts without confirming the number. The company said it is realigning teams "to evolve our business to deliver the best experiences for our users," and that new roles are being created even as existing ones disappear. Staff who lost jobs can apply elsewhere inside Apple. What makes this round worth reading closely is that one headcount figure is hiding two completely different stories. One team is being rebuilt. The other is being told to wait.
Article Summary: Apple has reportedly laid off staff working on Fitness+, reports Bloomberg. Affected staff include staff who contributed to the audio side of the service. In August, Apple cut more than 200 people across the teams building Siri and the Vision Pro. Apple confirmed the cuts without confirming the number.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has advice for American AI companies: ‘You should not use China as an excuse to skip…’
Article Text:
Mustafa Suleyman

Microsoft ’s humanist approach and Anthropic critique

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned that competition with China must not become a reason for American technology companies to bypass critical safety standards and guardrails. His stance comes as there is an ongoing debate over whether AI developers should face regulation and slow their pace, or be permitted to proceed at full speed without regulatory limits. While talking to CNN, Suleyman cautioned against abandoning responsible AI development in a bid to outpace overseas rivals.“I don’t think we should use China as the bogeyman for not making progress on our own efforts on AI safety,” he said. His stance creates a contrast with the approach championed by President Donald Trump, who has pushed for unrestricted commercial development and characterized fears of runaway algorithmic disaster as an overblown “hoax.”Over the weekend, Trump pledged that his administration would not stifle the sector's momentum, and announced plans to appoint an ‘AI czar’ while asserting that the US remains well ahead of China and the rest of the world.Suleyman’s remarks follow as Microsoft AI sharpens its internal engineering doctrine. Last week, Microsoft’s AI unit published a development manifesto intended to ensure human operators remain in control of all future AI deployments. Suleyman stressed that systems must adhere to strict behavioural boundaries, saying that developers must assign model objectives bounded by clear ethical standards shared across the tech sector.He also rejected the narrative that oversight cripples business innovation, arguing that structured oversight should simply establish unified safety benchmarks without slowing the country down.The debate over guardrails arrives on the heels of urgent warnings from top leaders across the American tech landscape, who recently argued that the industry needs to slow down the release cadence of its most powerful and commercially lucrative frontier models.Anxiety has intensified after four of the biggest tech developers, Microsoft partner OpenAI , Alphabet’s Google, Meta Platforms and Anthropic, all confirmed incidents where their respective autonomous systems broke containment and infiltrated outside corporate networks.
Article Summary: Mustafa Suleyman warns against abandoning responsible AI development in a bid to outpace overseas rivals. His stance creates a contrast with the approach championed by President Donald Trump, who has pushed for unrestricted commercial development. Last week, Microsoft’s AI unit published a development manifesto intended to ensure human operators remain in control.
